newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rebounds to end at 8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rebounds to end at 8.5 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate dropped to a low of 7.5 percent but firmed back to 8.5 percent due to borrowing by small banks and finance companies, dealers said on Friday.
"It fell to 7.5 percent from 8.5 and then went up all the way back to 8.5 because of presence of bad names," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Small banks and finance firms which are considered higher risk borrowers in the market are dubbed "bad names".
The overnight rate, which traded between 8.0 and 8.8 percent on Thursday, was expected to ease due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday, dealers said.
Earlier, interbank rates were steady as the market remained short of funds.
One-week money was unchanged at 8.70/80 percent.
One-month money at 8.60/70 percent and three-month at 8.30/50 percent, were also unchanged.
Dealers and analysts said rates could be heading lower after Bank Negara asked banks to hold their base lending rates steady despite the recent spike upward in interbank rates.
"Bank Negara will have to bring rates down," said Jimmy Koh, an economist at I.D.E.A. in Singapore. "If not, banks will suffer and will likely pass on the cost of funding to corporates."
There was no sign of Bank Negara lending on Friday, dealers said. The central bank has been injecting fresh funds into the market for the past two weeks to help ease the tight liquidity.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had left the domestic banking system heavily short of funds.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were up across the board on expectations of a softening in interbank rates, futures market dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up four points to 92.22, or an implied yield of 7.78 percent.
The December contract was also up four to 92.50, or 7.50 percent.
